title: Cisco a Better Bet Than Apple, Amazon, Tech Giants: Piper Jaffray
summary: Piper Jaffray's Chief Market Technician Craig Johnson argues that Cisco Systems (CSCO) is a better investment than tech giants like Apple (AAPL) and Amazon (AMZN), which may need a pullback. Johnson suggests buying Cisco due to its recent breakout from a consolidation range, anticipating a run to the $51-$52 range. He views Cisco as a value play, currently trading under $50 with a modest market capitalization.

title: Amazon.com users reported problems with search on the website Wednesday afternoon
summary: Thousands of Amazon.com users reported issues searching the online retailer for products on Wednesday, according to Down Detector and social media. The search outage, which affected desktop, mobile, and app users, began around 4 p.m. EDT. By 5:30 p.m., search functionality was restored, and Amazon Help stated that search "seems to work fine."

title: Walmart Relies on Crowdsourcing to Complete Grocery Delivery's Last Mile
summary: Walmart Inc. is piloting a new grocery delivery technology called Spark Delivery, which uses crowdsourcing to reduce last-mile delivery costs and offer flexible schedules for drivers. The program, powered by Bringg and managed by Delivery Drivers Inc., aims to expand to 100 metropolitan areas, covering 40% of U.S. households, and is comparable to Amazon's Flex service. This initiative follows a previous crowdsourcing program where Walmart associates delivered online orders on their way home.

title: Amazon Expands in San Diego, Opens 85K-SF Tech Hub at Alexandria’s Campus Pointe
summary: Amazon is expanding its San Diego Tech Hub by opening an 85,000-square-foot office at Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.’s Campus Pointe. This expansion is expected to create 300 new high-tech jobs in various fields including software development and machine learning. The new facility will allow Amazon to more than double its tech workforce in the area, contributing to the development of key Amazon services and products.

title: Report: 87 companies control world agricultural production
summary: A new report, the Agrifood Atlas, reveals that 87 corporations worldwide control the global agribusiness supply chain, encompassing a wide range of companies from beverage and meat-packing giants to technology firms. This concentration of market power, especially among four major traders (ADM, Bunge, Cargill, Louis Dreyfus Company), is leading to increasing monoculture, threatening food sovereignty, degrading land, and causing social conflicts. The report also highlights the financialization of agricultural commodities, where speculative trading far outweighs actual production, further exacerbating these issues.

title: Oracle President Thomas Kurian tells employees he's taking 'extended' time off
summary: Thomas Kurian, President of Oracle Corp., is taking an "extended" period of time off for unspecified reasons. Kurian leads the company's software development operations, overseeing approximately 35,000 engineers, which represents nearly a quarter of Oracle's total workforce.

title: Plug Power Moves Into Saratoga County With New Manufacturing Plant In Clifton Park
summary: Plug Power Inc., a manufacturer of hydrogen-powered fuel cells, opened a new 38,400-square-foot manufacturing plant in Clifton Park, New York, in August 2018. This expansion, costing nearly $2.8 million over five years, is set to create 97 new jobs and supplement their existing Latham facility. The company will receive approximately $640,000 in tax credits through New York State's Excelsior Job Program due to its commitment to job creation and continued innovation in clean energy.

title: Prologis buys 10-acre Pepsi plant near Mount Baker light rail station
summary: Logistics company Prologis has acquired a 10-acre Pepsi plant situated near the Mount Baker light rail station in Seattle. This purchase aligns with Prologis' strategy to address Amazon.com's increasing demand for in-city distribution space. The acquisition is part of a broader trend of Prologis buying commercial properties with a focus on "last mile" logistics.

title: Gartner Hype Cycle for Data Management Positions Three Technologies in the Innovation Trigger Phase in 2018
summary: Gartner's 2018 Hype Cycle for Data Management identifies DataOps, private cloud database platform as a service (dbPaaS), and machine learning (ML)-enabled data management as entering the Innovation Trigger phase. This indicates these technologies are generating significant interest, with a strong focus on execution and cloud-first delivery models in the data management space. The report highlights that while DataOps and ML-enabled data management are in nascent stages, dbPaaS is rapidly approaching mainstream adoption, especially for organizations with specific security or regulatory needs.

title: 5 lessons of the AI imperative, from Netflix to Spotify
summary: This article discusses the increasing importance of artificial intelligence and algorithms in business, using Netflix and Spotify as key examples. It highlights how companies are committing to AI to enhance efficiency, customer experience, and competitive advantage. The author emphasizes that understanding and leveraging AI is crucial for businesses across various sectors to thrive in the current technological landscape.

title: Sonos gets IFTTT support: Here are the new things your smart speakers can now do
summary: Sonos smart speakers now integrate with IFTTT, allowing them to be part of automated smart home routines. This integration enables features like music pausing during phone calls or doorbell rings, and starting/stopping music based on user location. Sonos is positioning itself as a platform-agnostic company, working with various smart home ecosystems.

title: Cheetos Restaurant Is The Flamin' Hottest Reservation In Hollywood
summary: Cheetos is opening a new, limited-time restaurant called The Flamin' Hot Spot in Los Angeles, dedicated to the flavor of Flamin' Hot Cheetos. The restaurant, curated by chef Roy Choi, will open from September 18-20 and offer a three-course menu featuring Cheetos-infused dishes. This follows the success of last year's Cheetos restaurant, The Spotted Cheetah, due to overwhelming fan demand for Cheetos culinary experiences.

summary: This article provides detailed information on the Amplify Lithium & Battery Technology ETF (BATT), including its current stock price, historical data, and key statistics. It also features recent news and analysis related to the ETF, technical analysis summaries, and its top holdings. The fund invests in companies involved in lithium battery technologies, battery storage solutions, and electric vehicles.

title: Amazon's rising stock gives Jeff Bezos 'financial muscle' in outer space equal to whole countries
summary: Morgan Stanley highlights Jeff Bezos' growing financial power through his Amazon shares, which he dedicates significantly to his space company, Blue Origin. His substantial wealth gives Blue Origin a unique advantage in the burgeoning space industry, potentially accelerating its development and competition with companies like SpaceX. Morgan Stanley advises investors to recognize Bezos' increasing influence in the space economy.

title: Amazon Investigates Employees Leaking Data for Bribes
authors: ['Jon Emont in Hong Kong and Laura Stevens and Robert McMillan in San Francisco']
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is investigating suspected data leaks and bribery involving its employees, particularly impacting its online marketplace in China. These employees, often through intermediaries, are reportedly selling internal data, reviewer email addresses, and services to remove negative reviews or reinstate banned accounts to independent merchants for prices ranging from $80 to over $2,000. This practice helps merchants gain an unfair advantage in sales and violates company policy, with the high volume of sellers and relatively low salaries among Amazon China employees cited as contributing factors.

title: Time Magazine Is Bought by Marc Benioff, Salesforce Billionaire (Published 2018)
summary: Marc Benioff, the co-founder of Salesforce, and his wife, Lynne, have agreed to purchase Time magazine from Meredith Corporation for $190 million. This acquisition marks another instance of a tech billionaire investing in an iconic media brand, following Jeff Bezos's purchase of The Washington Post and Laurene Powell Jobs's stake in The Atlantic. The Benioffs emerged as the preferred buyers due to their commitment to journalistic integrity amidst the struggles faced by the magazine industry.

title: |'America's Fittest CEO' Strauss Zelnick Develops Stellar Health & Fitness Plan In 'Becoming Ageless'
summary: |Strauss Zelnick, known as "America's Fittest CEO" at 61, has released a book titled 'Becoming Ageless: The Four Secrets to Looking and Feeling Younger Than Ever.' The book details his health and fitness plan, drawing from years of research into longevity science. It offers readers strategies for losing weight, enjoying healthy meals, and improving overall well-being.

title: Co-founder of Salesforce buys Time magazine for $190million
summary: Marc Benioff, co-founder of Salesforce, and his wife Lynne have purchased Time magazine for $190 million in cash from Meredith Corporation. The Benioffs will acquire Time personally, and the transaction is unrelated to Salesforce.com, with the couple stating they will not be involved in the day-to-day operations or journalistic decisions of the magazine. This acquisition continues a trend of wealthy tech giants acquiring traditional media institutions.

title: Salesforce's Benioff to Buy Time Magazine, Boosting Influence
summary: Marc Benioff, co-founder of Salesforce.com Inc., and his wife Lynne, are set to acquire Time magazine for $190 million in cash from Meredith Corp. This philanthropic purchase aims to boost Benioff's influence beyond Silicon Valley and enhance his public image. The deal draws comparisons to Jeff Bezos's acquisition of The Washington Post.

title: Salesforce co-founder Benioff buys Time magazine for $190 million
summary: Salesforce co-founder Marc Benioff and his wife, Lynne, have purchased Time magazine from Meredith Corp. for $190 million in cash. The acquisition is a personal investment by the Benioffs and is unrelated to Salesforce.com, continuing a trend of tech moguls acquiring legacy media publications. They will not be involved in the day-to-day operations or journalistic decisions, which will remain with Time's current executive leadership.

title: Jeff Bezos’ fortune is growing even faster than he can give it away
summary: Despite pledging $2 billion to his new charitable "Bezos Day One Fund", Jeff Bezos' personal fortune is continuing to grow at an accelerated pace due to the rising value of Amazon stock. His wealth increased by approximately $4 billion over the week, with a $500 million gain on Thursday alone, highlighting that his philanthropic efforts are currently outpaced by his wealth accumulation.

title: Marc Benioff, co-founder of Salesforce, buys Time magazine
summary: Salesforce co-founder Marc Benioff and his wife Lynne have purchased Time magazine from Meredith Corp. for $190 million. This acquisition is a personal investment by the Benioffs and continues a trend of tech titans buying traditional media outlets. The Benioffs will not be involved in the day-to-day operations or journalistic decisions of Time.

title: Amazon To Sell Insurance In India
summary: Amazon.com Inc. plans to enter the Indian insurance market by selling life, health, and general insurance policies through its Amazon Pay platform. This move aims to tap into India's highly underpenetrated insurance sector, projected to be worth $280 billion by 2020. Amazon is not the only tech giant making such a move, as Walmart-backed Flipkart and Paytm are also venturing into the Indian insurance space.

title: When an Owner’s New Company Puts the Old One in Trump’s Cross Hairs (Published 2018)
summary: Marc Benioff, co-founder and CEO of Salesforce, and his wife, Lynne, purchased Time magazine, raising questions about potential conflicts of interest and corporate governance in the age of President Trump. This acquisition could put Salesforce in the public and political spotlight, similar to how Amazon has been treated due to Jeff Bezos' ownership of The Washington Post. The article explores the implications of public company executives' extracurricular activities on their primary businesses.

title: Staples buys workplace vendor Essendant for $996M
summary: Staples acquired workplace product and services company Essendant for $996 million, including net debt, following a previous rejection of Staples' offer. This acquisition aligns with Staples' strategy to expand its business-to-business services amid a contracting retail market and follows a previous purchase of HiTouch Business Services. The Federal Trade Commission later approved the merger with an agreement to establish a firewall between Staples’ B2B operations and Essendant’s wholesale business.

title: Amazon to Launch 8 New Alexa-Powered Devices: Report
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) is reportedly planning to launch at least eight new Alexa-powered smart home devices, including a voice-controlled microwave oven, an amplifier, and an in-car gadget. This expansion is expected to intensify competition with rivals like Apple, Alphabet, and Microsoft in the smart speaker market, and marks Amazon's significant entry into the home appliance space. The move aligns with CEO Jeff Bezos's vision of integrating Alexa more deeply into everyday life, further expanding Amazon's presence in the smart home ecosystem.

title: Netflix Stock Climbs After Streamer’s Record 23 Emmy Wins
summary: Netflix's stock saw a climb after the streaming giant secured a record 23 Emmy wins in 2018, tying with HBO. Investors responded positively, pushing shares up initially and closing 4.9% higher for the day. This rebound followed a recent decline in stock price after hitting an all-time high in July.

title: Ticketing platform Eventbrite stock rises on debut day
summary: Eventbrite (NYSE: EB), the online ticketing solutions provider, saw its stock rise significantly by 58.70% on its debut day, closing at $36.50 after an IPO price of $23 per share. The company, which raised $230 million, reported a net revenue increase of 51% in 2017 to $201.6 million but registered a net loss of $38.5 million. Despite concerns over profitability and competition from major players like Live Nation, Amazon, and Facebook, Eventbrite aims to expand its market presence and category offerings.

title: Hair-care Veteran Andy Rah Cooks Up New Line
summary: Hair-care veteran Andy Rah is launching Sauce Beauty, an eight-item line of hair products inspired by food ingredients like Greek yogurt and avocado. The collection will debut exclusively at Sally Beauty on October 1st, with plans for broader mass market and international expansion, including its own website and Amazon. Rah aims to bring luxury hair care quality with a value price point, leveraging food-driven hair-care trends and social media interest.

title: Comcast outbids Fox and Walt Disney Co. with $40-billion offer for Europe’s Sky TV
summary: Comcast won a bidding war for Europe's Sky TV, offering nearly $40 billion, outbidding 21st Century Fox and Walt Disney Co. This acquisition significantly expands Comcast's global customer base, especially in prosperous European countries. The victory is a strategic boost for Comcast, which had previously vied with Disney for Fox assets.

title: Televisa anuncia la creación de Televisa Alternative Original (TAO)
summary: Grupo Televisa announced the launch of Televisa Alternative Originals (TAO), a new premium content division focused on developing, producing, and distributing Latin American and multicultural stories. TAO has signed a distribution agreement with Amazon Prime Video for several series, granting Amazon global SVOD rights while Televisa retains rights for its open television and pay television platforms in Mexico and through Univision in the U.S. This initiative aims to fill a market gap in the streaming industry by leveraging Latin American talent and multicultural stories.

title: JPMorgan Chase invests in agile platforms, digital talent
summary: JPMorgan Chase is heavily investing in agile platforms, APIs, and microservices under CIO Lori Beer to drive digital transformation and improve customer and employee experiences. With a significant IT budget, the bank is focusing on building a digital business and attracting top talent in AI, machine learning, and blockchain to stay competitive and fend off digital disruption. The company is actively recruiting diverse talent and training individuals through programs like "Code for Good" and "Tech Connect" to stay at the forefront of technology.

title: Can Macy's new store concepts prevent closures?
summary: Macy's is implementing new store concepts like Backstage, Bluemercury, and Market @ Macy's to prevent further store closures and drive growth. Despite some positive signs, including three quarters of comparable-store sales growth, analysts remain cautious about the long-term sustainability of the comeback in a challenging retail environment. The article highlights both the innovative strategies being pursued by Macy's and the skepticism from financial analysts regarding their effectiveness.

title: Hotel Workers Fret Over a New Rival: Alexa at the Front Desk (Published 2018)
summary: Hotel workers, particularly at Marriott, are concerned about job displacement due to new technologies like facial recognition check-in systems. Union members across various roles are authorizing strikes, adding demands for worker protection from technological advancements alongside traditional wage and safety concerns. This highlights a new challenge for the service sector, which has historically been less impacted by automation than manufacturing.

title: Zebra unveils new in-store mobile scanner for retailers
summary: Zebra Technologies has introduced the PS20, a new Android-based mobile barcode scanner designed for both shoppers and store associates to facilitate in-store scanning and payment, bypassing traditional checkout lines. This sixth-generation personal shopping solution includes features like a microphone, front-facing camera, and Visible Light Communication (VLC) technology for indoor positioning and targeted offers. The device aims to enhance the in-store shopping experience by providing convenience, improving communication between staff and customers, and offering more accurate inventory tracking through VLC.

title: Why T-Mobile Is Rebranding MetroPCS to 'Metro by T-Mobile'
summary: T-Mobile is rebranding its MetroPCS prepaid wireless service to "Metro by T-Mobile" to attract a broader customer base. The change, effective in October 2018, includes new unlimited data plans with Google One and Amazon Prime, aiming to shed the stigma of prepaid service and emphasize its use of T-Mobile's network. This overhaul is not related to T-Mobile's potential merger with Sprint.

title: America’s biggest car retailer is no longer drug testing employees for marijuana
summary: AutoNation Inc., the largest automotive retailer in the U.S., has announced it will no longer drug test job applicants or current employees for marijuana use. This policy change, which secretly began two years ago, reflects a growing trend among companies to adapt to increased public support for marijuana legalization and a tight labor market. Other major companies are expected to follow suit as employers face challenges finding employees who can pass traditional drug tests.

title: What’s in a name, anyway? Kroger rebrands ClickList
summary: Kroger has rebranded its click-and-collect service, ClickList, to "Grocery Pickup" to provide more clarity for shoppers, especially with its expanding range of e-commerce options including home delivery and Ship. This move aims to simplify its offerings for customers amidst increasing competition in the online grocery market from companies like Walmart, Whole Foods, Target, and Albertsons. While the $5 fee for pickup orders may need to be reevaluated given competitors' free services, Kroger's primary goal remains customer retention and acquisition.

title: After reportedly butting heads with Larry Ellison, Oracle's top cloud executive is leaving the company
summary: Oracle's top cloud executive, Thomas Kurian, has officially resigned from the company after reports of disagreements with co-founder Larry Ellison over cloud strategy. Kurian's departure follows a temporary leave of absence and comes as Oracle's cloud strategy faces challenges and increased competition from rivals like Amazon Web Services and Microsoft. Kurian had a significant role in attempting to transition Oracle to the cloud era over his two decades at the company.
